has_valid_signed_op.meaning: relayer holds a valid 77-byte signed UserOperation for AtomWallet
has_valid_signed_op.checkpoint: before relayer rewrites the signature suffix

suffix_encodes_window.meaning: last 12 bytes of the 77-byte signature encode validUntil and validAfter metadata
suffix_encodes_window.checkpoint: before relayer rewrites the signature suffix

hash_excludes_signature.meaning: getUserOpHash hashes the UserOperation excluding the signature field
hash_excludes_signature.checkpoint: before relayer rewrites the signature suffix

window_authenticated.meaning: the validUntil/validAfter time window is covered by the owner's signature so it cannot be altered without invalidating the signature
window_authenticated.checkpoint: after signature validation of the submitted operation

signer_window_enforced.meaning: the signer's intended time restriction is enforced (window not left unauthenticated)
signer_window_enforced.checkpoint: after signature validation of the submitted operation

assumptions: The relayer rewrites the last 12 bytes of userOp.signature before submission.
The submitted operation is presented for signature validation by AtomWallet.
The owner signature over userOpHash and the stripped 65-byte rawSignature remains valid after the suffix rewrite.

unresolved.description: Report does not give concrete validUntil/validAfter values, so the window bounds are represented only by the qualitative suffix_encodes_window observable.
Report does not state whether the rewritten operation was actually executed; execution is described as a capability.

limitations: The window-authentication relation is encoded as grounded Boolean observables because the report omits numeric validUntil/validAfter definitions.
Only the i_window_not_enforced impact is formalized; stale execution and unauthorized actions are handled in separate passes.
